disclaimer: General information only, not financial advice. Nothing here considers your income, health, family or the policies you already hold.
This site is independent. It is not run by, paid by or affiliated with any insurer, adviser or government agency, and earns nothing from any plan.
The plain-English explanations simplify on purpose. The policy contract, its definitions and its exclusions decide every claim, not this summary.
Pitfalls and caveats without a source link are general guidance written for this site, not official statements. Items with a link come from that source.
Plans, premiums and government rules change. Facts were checked on the date shown at the bottom of each page and may be out of date when you read them.
Savings, endowment, investment-linked, annuity and wealth or legacy plans are left out on purpose. A plan missing here may still be sold.

Before you buy, switch or cancel a policy, read the insurer's product summary and policy wording, and speak to a licensed financial adviser. Do not cancel existing cover until the new policy is in force.

schemes.name: MediShield Life
schemes.who: All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, for life.

key.l: claim limit per policy year, with no lifetime limit
inpatient deductible, rising in two phases: 1 Apr 2025 and 1 Apr 2027
new outpatient deductible from 1 Jun 2026

facts.t: Covers you for life regardless of age or pre-existing conditions.
Sized for Class B2/C bills in public hospitals.
Claim limit of $200,000 per policy year, with no lifetime limit.
Inpatient deductible rising by up to $1,500 in two phases: 1 April 2025 and 1 April 2027.
A $500-a-year outpatient deductible starts 1 June 2026 (moved from 1 January 2026).
Outpatient cover is limited to listed treatments such as cancer drug treatment, radiotherapy and kidney dialysis ($1,750 per month).
Excludes maternity charges (except listed serious complications), cosmetic surgery, dental work (except accidental injury), overseas treatment and private nursing.
Premiums are fully payable by MediSave.

schemes.name: CareShield Life
schemes.who: Automatic for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, from age 30. Optional for those born in 1979 or earlier.

key.l: for life, for a claim made in 2026
daily activities you must be unable to do before it pays
payout growth from 2026 to 2030 ($806 a month for a 2030 claim)

facts.t: Pays monthly cash for life while you cannot do at least 3 of 6 activities of daily living (severe disability).
A successful claim in 2026 pays $689 a month for life.
Payouts grow 4% a year from 2026 to 2030 (up from 2%); a claim in 2030 would pay $806 a month.
Payouts rise each year until you turn 67 or claim, whichever is earlier.
Premiums are paid until age 67 (or 10 years after joining, whichever is later), then cover continues for life.
Annual premium increases from 2026 to 2030 are moderated to about $38 on average and no more than $75.
Fully payable by MediSave; nobody loses cover for being unable to pay.

schemes.name: ElderShield
schemes.who: People enrolled before 2020. No longer open to new applications.

key.l: a month, for up to 60 or 72 months depending on the plan

facts.t: ElderShield 300 pays $300 a month for up to 60 months; ElderShield 400 pays $400 a month for up to 72 months.
Premiums are fixed at entry and paid until the policy anniversary after age 65.
Run by the Government since 1 November 2021.

schemes.name: Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS)
schemes.who: Working Singapore Citizens and PRs aged 21 to 65 with CPF contributions; those aged 16 to 20 can apply.

key.l: cover for death, terminal illness or TPD up to age 59, then S$55,000 for 5 more years
premium, paid from your CPF savings

facts.t: Covers death, terminal illness and total permanent disability.
Sum assured S$70,000 up to age 59, then S$55,000 for the next 5 years.
Premiums start from S$18 a year and are paid from CPF savings.
Administered solely by Great Eastern Life.
Optional: you can opt out, but re-joining later depends on your health then.

schemes.name: Home Protection Scheme (HPS)
schemes.who: HDB flat owners paying their housing loan with CPF (required) or cash (encouraged).

key.l: or until the HDB loan is paid off
private property, ECs and privatised HUDC flats are not covered

facts.t: Pays off the outstanding housing loan on your HDB flat, up to the insured sum, on death, terminal illness or total permanent disability. It covers an HDB loan or a bank loan.
quote: settle the outstanding housing loan, up to the insured sum, with HDB or the mortgagee directly
If you're taking a bank loan, you can submit an online application to apply for HPS

facts.t: Covers you until age 65 or until the loan is paid off.
Does not cover private property, executive condominiums or privatised HUDC flats.
Each household's shares of cover must add up to at least 100%.
Premiums are deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account; acceptance depends on your health.

categories.name: Hospitalisation (Shield and medical plans)
categories.short: Pays large hospital bills. Upgrades MediShield Life to A/B1 wards or private hospitals.
categories.plain: If you are warded in hospital, this pays most of the bill. Every Singapore Citizen and PR already has MediShield Life, which is sized for subsidised B2 and C wards in public hospitals. A Shield plan adds a private layer on top, so a bigger bill from an A ward or a private hospital is still mostly covered. Example: you choose a private hospital for an operation. With MediShield Life alone you would pay most of the difference yourself. A private-hospital Shield plan is built for that bill, though you still pay a {{deductible}} and a {{co-payment}}.
categories.who: Almost everyone. It is the cover that protects you from a very large hospital bill. Pick the ward class you would really use: a higher class costs more every year, and the gap grows as you age.

key.l: most MediSave pays a year for the private part, by age next birthday: 40 and below / 41 to 70 / 71 up. Rest is cash.
key.quote: based on your age next birthday

key.l: your MediShield Life premium: what a Shield plan can cost in your 70s or 80s
to cancel a new Shield plan after you receive it (the free-look period)

categories.what: An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is MediShield Life plus a private top-up from an insurer. The private part targets higher ward classes or private hospitals and lets you choose your doctor. Some insurers also sell international or regional medical plans that are not Shield plans; those are tagged, and are not on MOH's list of MediSave-approved Shield plans.

facts.t: Seven insurers sell IPs: AIA, Great Eastern, HSBC Life, Income, Prudential, Raffles Health Insurance and Singlife.
You can hold only one IP at a time.
MediSave pays the private part only up to $300 a year (age 40 and below next birthday), $600 (41 to 70) or $900 (71 and above). The rest is cash.
IP premiums rise with age and could be up to five times your MediShield Life premiums in your 70s or 80s.
Standard IPs have the same coverage at every insurer; other IPs differ.
69% of private-component claims that paid nothing were bills at or below the deductible.

watch.t: Pre-existing conditions may be excluded from the private part, though MediShield Life still covers them.
watch.quote: even if your pre-existing conditions are not covered under the additional portion

watch.t: Using an insurer's {{panel-doctor|panel doctors}} usually means lower co-payment and {{pre-authorisation}}. Check the panel before you need it.
Switching Shield plans can cost you cover: conditions you already have are then covered only up to MediShield Life benefits. Do not cancel the old plan until the new one is in force.
watch.quote: you will only be covered for pre-existing conditions up to MediShield Life benefits

watch.t: Choosing a plan you cannot afford after you retire. Premiums rise with age, MediSave covers only part of the private premium, and the rest is cash.
Letting the plan lapse over a missed payment. Buying again later means new health checks, and anything you developed in between can be excluded.

caveats.t: It pays back real bills, up to its limits. It does not give you cash for being ill.
You pay a deductible once each policy year, then a co-payment. From 1 April 2026, new riders cannot cover the minimum deductible.
caveats.quote: This ranges from $1,500 to $3,500 per policy year

caveats.t: Overseas treatment is excluded from MediShield Life, so any overseas cover depends entirely on the insurer's private part.
Plans tagged "Not a Shield plan" are international or regional medical plans. They are not on MOH's list of MediSave-approved Shield plans.

compare: Ward class targeted (B1, A or private)
Lifetime premium at your age (MOH publishes this)

categories.name: IP riders
categories.short: Optional add-on to an IP that pays part of your co-payment.
categories.plain: Even with a Shield plan, you pay part of each hospital bill yourself: first a {{deductible}}, then a {{co-payment}} on the rest. A rider is an add-on that pays some of your share. Under the rules for riders sold from 1 April 2026, you still pay the deductible and at least 5% of the rest, but your yearly co-payment is capped if you use panel doctors or get pre-authorisation.
categories.who: People who want a predictable worst-case hospital bill and can afford a yearly premium paid in cash on top of the Shield plan.

key.l: minimum yearly deductible that new riders cannot cover from 1 Apr 2026 ($3,500 for Class A or private)
minimum yearly co-payment cap, for panel or pre-authorised claims only
minimum co-payment on every claim, unchanged

categories.what: A rider sits on top of your Integrated Shield Plan and reduces what you pay yourself after a claim. Rules changed for riders sold from 1 April 2026.

facts.t: From 1 April 2026, new riders cannot cover the minimum IP deductible.
Minimum deductibles range from $1,500 to $3,500 a year depending on ward class ($3,500 for Class A or private).
The yearly co-payment cap rose to a minimum of $6,000, excluding the deductible, and applies only to panel or pre-authorised claims.
The minimum 5% co-payment is unchanged.
New riders are expected to cost about 30% less than older full-coverage riders.
Riders bought from 27 November 2025 to 31 March 2026 move to the new design no later than the next renewal after 1 April 2028.

watch.t: Riders bought before 27 November 2025 are left to each insurer to decide. Ask yours what will happen.
Dropping an older rider to save money is usually one-way. New riders sold from 1 April 2026 cannot cover the minimum deductible, so the old design cannot be bought again.
Paying for a rider and then using non-panel doctors without pre-authorisation. The co-payment cap applies only to panel or pre-authorised claims.

caveats.t: Rider premiums are paid in cash, not MediSave, and they rise with age.
caveats.quote: The premium for riders must be paid with cash

caveats.t: A rider sits on that insurer's own Shield plan. If you switch Shield plans to another insurer, the old rider does not come with you.

metrics.label: Attaches to
metrics.why: The Shield plan or tier it must sit on.

metrics.label: Co-payment cap
metrics.why: Most you pay in co-payment a year.

metrics.label: Panel condition
metrics.why: When the cap or cover needs the insurer's doctors.

categories.name: Term life
categories.short: Lump sum to your family if you die or are totally disabled within a set period.
categories.plain: You pay a premium for a fixed period, for example until age 65. If you die or become {{tpd|totally and permanently disabled}} in that period, your family gets a lump sum. If nothing happens, the cover simply ends and you get nothing back. That is why it is the cheapest way to buy a large amount of cover. Example: a parent with young children and a home loan buys cover that lasts until the youngest child is grown up and the loan is paid off.
categories.who: Anyone whose death would leave others short of money: children, a partner, parents you support, or debts shared with someone. If nobody relies on your income, you may need little or none.

key.l: death and TPD cover: the MoneySense rule of thumb
average death cover per policyholder in 2022 (LIA study)
key.quote: approximately 3.6 times of average annual income

key.l: DPS cover many working CPF members already have, up to age 59

categories.what: Protection for a fixed period, usually to an age like 65 or 75. It pays only if a claim happens in that period and has no cash value.

facts.t: Term insurance pays the sum insured only on death or total and permanent disability during the term, and is typically cheaper because it has no savings element.
A rule of thumb: death and TPD cover of 9 times your annual income.
Direct Purchase Insurance (DPI) term plans are sold without advice or commission, so premiums are lower. Their names start with "DIRECT".
Working CPF members aged 21 to 65 are automatically covered by DPS (S$70,000 up to age 59) unless they opt out.

watch.t: {{decreasing-term|Decreasing (mortgage) term}} cover shrinks over the term and reaches zero at the end, so it is built for a debt that shrinks, such as a home loan.
quote: will reduce and become zero by the end of the term
those used to cover the default of a housing loan

watch.t: Paying twice for mortgage cover. On an HDB flat, {{hps|HPS}} pays off the housing loan, whether from HDB or a bank, and it is required if you pay the instalments with CPF. Check what you already hold first. HPS does not cover private property or ECs.
quote: If you're using CPF savings to pay your monthly housing instalments, HPS is required
If you're taking a bank loan, you can submit an online application to apply for HPS
HPS does not cover private residential properties, such as executive condominiums

watch.t: Renewable term plans re-price at each renewal and can get expensive late in life.
Buying cover that ends too early. A plan to 65 pays nothing at 66, so match the end age to when your family stops depending on you.
Forgetting cover you already have. DPS counts; cover from an employer usually stops when you leave the job.
Leaving out health facts on the application. Usually for the first one or two years the insurer can treat the policy as if it was never issued, and after that it can still end it if fraud is proven.

caveats.t: There is no cash value. If you stop paying, the cover ends and nothing is returned.
Suicide within a period stated in the policy is not paid.
What counts as total and permanent disability differs between insurers and can change at older ages. Read the policy's definition.
TPD cover is not an income. Disability income insurance works differently.
caveats.label: Compare TPD with disability income

compare: Whether TPD and terminal illness are included
Option to convert or increase cover without health checks

metrics.label: Entry age
metrics.why: Ages at which you can start it.

metrics.label: Total and permanent disability
metrics.why: Pays if you can never work again.

metrics.label: Terminal illness
metrics.why: Pays early on a terminal diagnosis.

metrics.label: Premium rates
metrics.why: Guaranteed means they cannot be raised.

metrics.label: Renew, convert or increase without health checks
metrics.why: Keeps cover if your health changes.

categories.name: Whole life
categories.short: Lifelong cover that pays out whenever you die. Costs much more than term.
categories.plain: Cover that lasts your whole life, so it will pay out one day as long as you keep the policy going. Part of each premium builds a cash value inside the policy, which is why it costs much more than term cover for the same payout. Many plans add a "multiplier" that boosts your cover up to an age such as 70, then drops back to the basic amount.
categories.who: People who want a payout whenever they die, for example to leave money to someone, and can afford the higher premium for many years. If your main aim is protecting your family during your working years, term cover gives far more cover for the money.

key.l: the most to spend on protection. Bundled plans like whole life may go past it.
most the PPF Scheme protects in guaranteed sum assured, per life per insurer, if an insurer fails

categories.what: Whole life covers you for life and builds a cash value. Plans sold mainly as savings, income, wealth or legacy products, including universal and indexed universal life, are left out of this site.

facts.t: Whole life pays the sum insured plus bonuses on death or TPD; premiums can be limited to a set period.
Bonuses are non-guaranteed: your return can underperform expectations.
Bundled products like whole life may push premiums above 15% of income because they mix savings and protection.

watch.t: Ending the policy early loses money, and cash values build up only after a minimum period.
watch.quote: Early termination causes you to lose money

watch.t: The Policy Owners' Protection Scheme only protects guaranteed benefits, capped at S$500,000 sum assured and S$100,000 surrender value per life per insurer.
Treating it as a savings account. The cash value grows slowly, may not be guaranteed, and taking it out ends or shrinks your cover.
Multiplier cover drops after the multiplier age, often when your health makes new cover hard to buy. Know what cover remains after that age.
Committing to a premium you cannot keep up for decades. Stopping early is where whole life loses the most money.

caveats.t: If you miss a premium after the grace period, the insurer may pay it with a loan against your cash value. That loan charges interest.
A policy loan against the cash value charges interest and reduces what is paid out if it is not repaid.
Suicide within a period stated in the policy is not paid.
In the Policy Illustration, look at the guaranteed figures. The higher projected figures depend on non-guaranteed bonuses.

compare: Multiplier: extra cover until a set age

categories.name: Critical illness (CI)
categories.short: Lump sum on diagnosis of a listed serious illness, to replace income while you recover.
categories.plain: If you are diagnosed with a serious illness on the policy's list, such as a major cancer, heart attack or stroke, it pays you a lump sum. The money is yours to use however you need: living costs while you cannot work, treatment your Shield plan does not cover, or care at home. It does not depend on your hospital bill.
categories.who: People whose household would struggle if they could not earn for a year or more while recovering.

key.l: critical illness cover: the MoneySense rule of thumb
average CI cover per policyholder in 2022 (LIA study)
key.quote: approximately 2.1 times of average annual income

key.l: typical waiting period after you buy, for illnesses such as major cancers and heart attack

categories.what: CI plans pay a lump sum on diagnosis, not a reimbursement of bills. Some pay only at the severe stage; {{early-stage-ci|early or multi-stage}} plans pay earlier; {{multi-pay}} plans pay more than once.

facts.t: LIA standardises the severe-stage definitions of 37 critical illnesses so claims are judged the same way at every insurer.
LIA updated these definitions in 2024. From 1 October 2025, plans using the older Version 2019 definitions may no longer be sold, so a CI plan you buy now uses Version 2024 for those illnesses.
facts.quote: Starting from 1 October 2025, products using the Version 2019 definitions may no longer be sold in Singapore

facts.t: The 2024 review changed 7 of the 37 definitions and left 30 unchanged, to keep up with medical practice and remove unclear wording.
quote: The definitions of 7 CIs were updated whilst 30 definitions remained unchanged
aligned with advances made in medical technology and medical practice as well as to address areas of ambiguity

facts.t: Two changes a buyer may notice: Major Cancer now names pituitary tumours (PitNET) as excluded, which LIA says were never meant to be covered; and heart valve surgery no longer needs the chest wall to be opened, though keyhole and catheter procedures are still not covered.
quote: PitNET covers pituitary adenoma which was not classified previously as Cancer and never intended to be covered under Major Cancer definition
This revised definition no longer requires opening of chest wall
The operation or procedure performed via endoscopic or keyhole surgery
The operation or procedure performed via catheterisation

facts.t: A policy you already hold keeps the definitions in its own contract, and you cannot ask for it to be moved to the new ones. When you renew or increase cover, the insurer may apply the new definitions: ask yours.
quote: your existing policy contract is not impacted
such an update is not possible
Insurers can choose to apply the latest definitions in respect of existing policy renewals
Insurers can choose to apply the latest definitions to the increased coverage portion

facts.t: LIA's example: a $100,000 policy bought in 2020 and topped up by $50,000 in 2026. A claim in 2028 is assessed on Version 2019 for the $100,000 and Version 2024 for the $50,000.
quote: Applying Version 2019 to $100,000
Applying Version 2024 to $50,000

facts.t: Early and intermediate stages are not defined by LIA; each insurer sets its own.
A rule of thumb: CI cover of 4 times your annual income.

watch.t: Early-stage definitions vary. Read the policy's list, not the marketing count of conditions.
A CI benefit that accelerates your life policy reduces your death cover when it pays.
Treating it as hospital cover. CI pays a lump sum to you; your Shield plan pays the bills. Most people need both.
Buying multi-pay cover without checking the waiting time between claims and whether a relapse of the same illness counts.

caveats.t: It pays only when the diagnosis meets the policy's definition and stage. Being seriously ill is not enough on its own.
Most plans have a waiting period, typically 90 days from the start of cover, for illnesses such as major cancers and heart attack. A diagnosis inside it is not paid.
caveats.quote: typically 90 days from the date the insurance coverage commences

caveats.t: Conditions you had before buying are usually excluded.

metrics.label: Stages covered
metrics.why: Early-stage cover pays sooner than severe-only.

metrics.label: Conditions covered
metrics.why: Count as the insurer states it.

metrics.label: Number of claims
metrics.why: One payout, or several and up to what cap.

metrics.label: Entry age
metrics.why: Ages at which you can start it.

metrics.label: Waiting period
metrics.why: Time after cover starts before some claims count.

categories.name: Cancer plans
categories.short: Lump sum (or yearly payouts) on cancer diagnosis only.
categories.plain: A cheaper, narrower kind of critical illness cover that pays only if you are diagnosed with cancer. Many pay from an early stage, and some pay every year while treatment continues. It pays nothing for a heart attack, stroke or any other illness.
categories.who: People who already have hospital cover and want a cash buffer for cancer specifically, or who cannot afford full critical illness cover yet.

key.l: a month: MediShield Life's limit for outpatient cancer drugs, and only for drugs on MOH's Cancer Drug List

categories.what: A narrower, cheaper form of critical illness cover that pays only for cancer, often from early stage.

facts.t: Outpatient cancer drug treatment under MediShield Life is limited to drugs on MOH's Cancer Drug List, at $200 to $12,800 a month depending on the drug.
IP claim limits for cancer drugs are set by each private insurer.

watch.t: Cancer-only cover does not pay for heart attack, stroke or other critical illnesses.
Many cancer plans are yearly renewable and their premiums are not guaranteed.
Buying it instead of full critical illness cover to save money, then falling ill with something that is not cancer.

caveats.t: What counts as {{early-stage-ci|early-stage}} cancer is set by each insurer, not by a common standard.
MediShield Life pays for outpatient cancer drugs only if they are on MOH's Cancer Drug List. Cash from a cancer plan can help with drugs outside it.
A waiting period after you buy is common. A diagnosis inside it is not covered.

compare: Whether it also pays for Cancer Drug List gaps

categories.name: Disability income
categories.short: Monthly income if illness or injury stops you working.
categories.plain: If illness or injury stops you working for a long time, this pays you a monthly income, usually a share of your earnings, until you recover or the benefit period ends. Think of it as insuring your salary rather than your life.
categories.who: People who live on their own earnings and have little savings to fall back on, especially the self-employed, who have no employer sick leave.

key.l: of your average monthly salary: the usual most it pays
or until age 60 or 65: how long payouts usually last

categories.what: Replaces part of your income if you become totally or partially disabled and cannot work, under the policy's conditions.

facts.t: Disability income insurance helps replace part of your income if you become totally or partially disabled and cannot work because of accident or sickness.
Long-term accident and health policies, including disability income, are protected by the PPF Scheme without caps.

watch.t: Check whether disability means unable to do your own job or any job. LIA calls the definition the most important thing to check.
watch.quote: The most important thing to consider when taking up disability income insurance is the definition of disability used in the policy

watch.t: Payouts usually start only after a {{deferred-period|deferred period}}, and only if you are still disabled then.
watch.quote: Benefits are payable only if you're continuously disabled after the deferred period

watch.t: Assuming {{tpd|TPD}} cover does the same job. A TPD definition such as DPS's needs the inability to take part in any employment permanently, so a long illness you recover from would not count.
watch.quote: the inability to take part in any employment permanently

watch.t: Insuring more than you earn. Payouts are capped at a share of your actual income, so extra cover cannot be claimed.
watch.quote: Pays up to 80% of your average monthly salary

caveats.t: Payouts usually stop at a set age stated in the policy, even if you are still disabled.
Some plans reduce the payout by other disability income you receive.
Few of the insurers here sell it to individuals. See "Who sells it" below.

compare: Benefit period and maximum % of income

versus.title: Disability income or TPD cover?
versus.intro: Both can pay when illness or injury stops you working, but they are built differently. This sets them side by side as the official guides describe them. Your policy's own wording decides any claim.
cols: TPD cover in a life plan

a.t: A fixed amount each month, to replace part of the income you lose.
a.quote: it pays a fixed amount each month to replace part of the income you would lose

b.t: The plan's sum insured, if you become totally and permanently disabled during the cover period.
b.quote: It pays the sum insured only if you die or become totally and permanently disabled

b.t: How the payout is scheduled varies by product and insurer.
b.quote: Payment schedules and definitions of disability vary across products and insurers

a.t: Usually no more than 80% of your average monthly salary.
a.quote: usually pays no more than 80% of your average monthly salary

b.t: The amount you chose. The MoneySense rule of thumb for death and TPD cover together is 9 times annual income.

a.t: Depends on the policy: some pay if you cannot do your usual work, others only if you cannot do any work at all.
a.quote: Some policies define disability as not being able to perform your usual work, while others define it as not being able to do any work at all

b.t: Total and permanent. DPS, for example, needs the inability to take part in any employment permanently, or the permanent loss of use of both eyes, two limbs, or one eye and one limb.
quote: the inability to take part in any employment permanently
the total permanent loss of physical function of both eyes, or two limbs, or one eye and one limb

a.t: After the deferred period, and only if you are still disabled then.
a.quote: Benefits are payable only if you're continuously disabled after the deferred period

b.t: For DPS, once a registered medical practitioner certifies the disability. Other plans set their own claim rules.
b.quote: certified by a registered medical practitioner

a.t: Usually up to 5 or 10 years, or until 60 or 65. It stops or falls once you can work again.
quote: The monthly income may be paid for up to 5 or 10 years, or until you are 60 or 65
Payment will stop or reduce once you can start work again

b.t: Only for a disability that happens while the plan is in force. A term plan pays nothing for one after its term ends.
b.quote: become totally and permanently disabled (if this benefit is provided) during this period

versus.scenarios_note: Made-up situations, to show how the rules above apply. Real outcomes depend on the policy wording.

scenarios.title: Off work for 18 months with a long illness, then back at work

items.t: Pays monthly once the deferred period has passed, then stops or falls when you can work again.
quote: Payment of benefits usually starts if you are disabled after the deferred period
Payment will stop or reduce once you can start work again

items.t: A disability that ends is not permanent, so it would not meet a definition like DPS's.
items.quote: the inability to take part in any employment permanently

scenarios.title: Can no longer do your own job, but could do other work

items.t: Turns on the definition: a policy that pays when you cannot do your usual work can pay; one that needs you unable to do any work may not.
items.quote: Some policies define disability as not being able to perform your usual work, while others define it as not being able to do any work at all

items.t: A definition like DPS's needs you permanently unable to take part in any employment, unless you have lost the use of both eyes, two limbs, or one eye and one limb.
quote: the inability to take part in any employment permanently
the total permanent loss of physical function of both eyes, or two limbs, or one eye and one limb

scenarios.title: Permanently unable to work at all

items.t: Can pay monthly until its benefit period ends, which may be 5 or 10 years, or age 60 or 65, even though you never recover.
items.quote: The monthly income may be paid for up to 5 or 10 years, or until you are 60 or 65

items.t: Can pay the plan's sum insured, as the disability is total and permanent.
items.quote: It pays the sum insured only if you die or become totally and permanently disabled

categories.name: Long-term care (CareShield supplements)
categories.short: Monthly cash if you become severely disabled, on top of CareShield Life.
categories.plain: If you become so disabled that you need help with daily basics like washing, dressing or eating, this pays you monthly cash for as long as that lasts. CareShield Life already does this for most Singaporeans born in 1980 or later. A supplement raises the monthly amount, and some start paying at a milder level of disability.
categories.who: People who want more than CareShield Life's base payout of $689 a month for a 2026 claim, for example to afford a helper or a nursing home.

key.l: what CareShield Life alone pays for a claim made in 2026
most MediSave pays towards supplement premiums, per insured person

categories.what: Supplements top up CareShield Life or ElderShield with higher monthly payouts, and some pay at milder disability levels.

facts.t: You must already be covered by CareShield Life or ElderShield to buy a supplement.
MediSave can pay supplement premiums up to $600 per calendar year per insured person, from your own or a family member's account.
Supplement insurers named by MOH: Singlife, Great Eastern and Income.
CareShield Life alone pays $689 a month for a claim made in 2026.

watch.t: CareShield Life only pays at 3 of 6 activities of daily living. Supplements that pay at 1 or 2 ADLs cost more.
Waiting until you are older to buy. Health checks get harder and some conditions will be excluded.
Assuming the monthly payout will cover care costs in full. Work out what a helper or nursing home costs first.

caveats.t: You must stay covered by CareShield Life or ElderShield for a supplement.
MediSave pays at most $600 a year per insured person towards supplement premiums. Anything above is cash.
Payouts start only after your disability is assessed and certified, which takes time.

compare: Monthly payout and how it grows

categories.name: Personal accident (PA)
categories.short: Pays for accidental death, disability and accident medical bills.
categories.plain: Cheap yearly cover for accidents only. It pays a lump sum if an accident kills or permanently disables you, and usually pays back medical bills from the accident, such as a clinic visit for a sprain, physiotherapy or TCM.
categories.who: Active people, people in jobs or hobbies with injury risk, and anyone who wants small accident bills covered. A Shield plan's deductible makes small bills hard to claim there.
categories.what: Cheap yearly cover for accidents only: a lump sum for accidental death or permanent disability, plus reimbursement of accident medical costs, often including TCM and physiotherapy.

facts.t: Personal accident is one of the accident and health policy types protected by the PPF Scheme.

watch.t: Illness is not covered, even if it leads to death or disability.
Many plans exclude or limit infectious diseases, high-risk sports and some occupations. Check the exclusions.
Relying on it as your life or disability cover. Most deaths and disabilities come from illness, which it never pays for.

caveats.t: It is renewed yearly, and the insurer can change the terms or premium at renewal.
Partial disability pays a set percentage from a table in the policy, not the full sum.

categories.name: Hospital cash (hospital income)
categories.short: Fixed daily cash for each day you are warded.
categories.plain: Pays you a fixed amount for each day you are warded, whatever the bill. The money is for the extras around a hospital stay: lost income, transport, someone to look after the children.
categories.who: People who would lose income while in hospital, such as the self-employed. It is a small extra on top of a Shield plan, never a replacement for one.

key.l: in hospital, whatever the bill. It may pay more or less than your actual costs.
key.quote: may be more or less than your actual expenses

categories.what: Pays a set amount per day in hospital, whatever the bill. Useful for lost income or extras, not for paying the bill itself.

facts.t: A hospital income plan pays a fixed daily benefit based on the number of days you are an inpatient.

watch.t: Short stays and day surgery often pay little or nothing. It does not replace an IP.
Paying for it when paid sick leave already covers your income.

caveats.t: Many plans set a minimum stay or a maximum number of days a year.
Conditions you had before buying are usually excluded.

categories.name: Maternity and child
categories.short: Pregnancy complications, congenital conditions and cover for newborns.
categories.plain: Maternity plans cover serious pregnancy complications and the baby's congenital conditions, which MediShield Life covers only partly. Bought during pregnancy, many let the baby keep cover after birth without health checks. Child plans are ordinary hospital, critical illness or accident plans taken out on a child.
categories.who: Expectant parents, ideally early in the pregnancy, and parents who want their child covered before any condition can show up.

key.l: MediSave Grant for Newborns from 1 Apr 2025. It fully covers a citizen baby's MediShield Life premiums to age 21.

categories.what: Maternity plans cover the mother and baby during pregnancy and early life; child plans cover hospitalisation, CI and accidents from birth.

facts.t: MediShield Life excludes routine maternity charges and Caesarean operations but covers a list of serious pregnancy and delivery complications.
The MediSave Grant for Newborns rose to $5,000 from 1 April 2025 and fully covers a citizen baby's MediShield Life premiums up to age 21.

watch.t: Maternity plans usually need to be bought by a set week of pregnancy. Check the cut-off early.
Buying a child's IP early locks in cover before any condition can be excluded.
Some maternity plans come bundled with an investment-linked or whole life policy for the child. Check what you will keep paying for years after the birth; you may only want the maternity part.

caveats.t: MediShield Life does not pay for a normal delivery or a Caesarean.
Problems already known before you buy, including in the current pregnancy, are usually excluded.

compare: Option to continue cover for the child without health checks

categories.name: Outpatient, GP and dental
categories.short: Clinic visits, specialist consults and dental. Mostly outside MediShield Life.
categories.plain: Pays part of everyday clinic bills: GP visits, specialist consultations, and sometimes dental or TCM. Hospital plans mostly do not cover these.
categories.who: Mainly people without outpatient benefits from an employer who see a doctor often. For most people, paying clinic bills from savings works out cheaper.

key.l: MediShield Life outpatient deductible from 1 Jun 2026, on the outpatient treatments it covers
in MediShield Life, unless the dental work is due to an accidental injury
key.quote: Dental work (except due to accidental injuries)

categories.what: Plans or riders that reimburse GP, specialist, TCM or dental visits. Few insurers sell these to individuals.

facts.t: MediShield Life's outpatient benefits are limited to listed treatments such as cancer treatment, dialysis and long-term parenteral nutrition.
Dental work is excluded from MediShield Life except treatment due to accidental injury.

watch.t: Premiums often cost close to what you would claim. Work out your yearly clinic spend first.
Paying for cover you already get from your employer.

caveats.t: Per-visit and yearly limits are low, and many plans pay only at panel clinics.
Regular check-ups for a long-term condition may be excluded.

compare: Panel clinics only or any clinic

categories.name: Riders (waiver, payor, CI add-ons)
categories.short: Add-ons to a main policy: waive premiums, add CI or TPD cover.
categories.plain: A rider is an optional add-on to a main policy. Common ones: a premium waiver, where your remaining premiums are paid for you if you get a critical illness or become disabled; a {{payor-rider|payor rider}}, which does the same on a child's policy if the parent paying for it is hit; and critical illness riders that add CI cover to a life plan.
categories.who: Useful when the main plan is long-term and would lapse if you could not pay. Compare the price with a standalone plan first.

key.l: riders pay out of the main policy's cover, and the policy may end once the rider pays
key.quote: If the rider accelerates the basic policy's benefit, the policy may expire after the rider is paid out

categories.what: For extra premium, a rider adds protection or enhances the main policy's benefits. Common ones waive future premiums if you (or the payer, for a child's policy) are diagnosed with CI or become disabled.

facts.t: A rider provides additional protection or enhances existing benefits for an extra premium.

watch.t: A rider usually ends when the main policy ends or lapses.
Accelerated CI riders pay from your death benefit, not on top of it.
Adding riders until the policy costs more than separate plans for the same cover would.

caveats.t: Riders often end at an earlier age than the main policy.
Some rider premiums are not guaranteed and can be raised.

starting_pay.who: Median gross monthly pay of fresh graduates from NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT and SUSS in full-time permanent jobs, surveyed in November 2025, about six months after their final exams. Before employee CPF; bonuses are not included.
quote: Gross monthly salary pertains only to full-time permanently employed graduates
bonuses, stock options, lump sum payments, and payments-in-kind are excluded
approximately six months after completing their final examinations

lines.t: The first part of a medical bill that you pay yourself before the insurance pays anything. You pay it once a policy year, not on every bill. Plans with lower premiums usually have higher deductibles.
quote: A deductible is the initial amount you have to pay for your medical expenses before your health insurance makes a payout
You usually only need to pay the deductible once in a policy year
Plans with lower premiums usually have higher deductibles

lines.t: For a Shield plan it is $1,500 to $3,500 a policy year, depending on the ward class.
lines.quote: ranging from $1,500 to $3,500, depending on ward class

example.t: MOH's example: Mr A has a knee replacement in a private hospital and the bill is $56,900. With a new rider he pays the $3,500 deductible, then 5% of the rest of the bill: $6,170 in all, which MediSave covers within its limits.
quote: incurs a bill of $56,900
pays the IP deductible of $3,500, followed by 5% of the remaining bill amount, totalling $6,170
This is entirely covered by MediSave, based on the applicable withdrawal limits

lines.t: After the deductible, the share of the rest of the bill that you still pay, usually a percentage. It is also called co-insurance.
quote: Co-insurance is how much you have to co-pay or split the cost with the insurer after you pay the deductible
It is usually expressed as a percentage

lines.t: Even with a Shield rider you still pay a co-payment: 5% of the bill, with a yearly cap of at least $6,000.
quote: Even with a rider, you will need to pay a deductible and a co-payment when you make a claim
The co-payment is 5% of the bill, capped at a minimum of $6,000 per year

lines.t: That cap applies only to panel or pre-authorised claims.
lines.quote: Co-payment cap only applies to eligible claims such as panel or pre-authorised claims

example.t: MoneySense's example: with a co-insurance of 10%, you pay 10% of the cost after the deductible.
example.quote: if you have a co-insurance of 10%, you will pay 10% of the cost after the deductible

lines.t: A benefit paid on the actual bill, with no claim limit for that benefit.
lines.quote: on an as-charged basis (i.e. no claim limit)

lines.t: You will see "As charged" in MOH's Shield plan tables on the Compare tab.

example.t: MOH's example: before 1 September 2022, MediShield Life paid up to $3,000 a month for cancer drugs, and Shield plans often paid the cost above that as charged, with a small co-payment. That has since changed.
quote: MediShield Life paid up to $3,000/month for all cancer drugs and Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) often covered costs above that on an as-charged basis
with a small co-payment

lines.t: The doctors and hospitals that work closely with your Shield insurer, called its main panel. Using them can mean pre-authorisation of claims and a lower co-payment.
quote: is referred to as an insurer's main panel
Policyholders can enjoy additional benefits like pre-authorisation of claims and lower co-payment when using these providers

lines.t: Under the Extended Panel, some specialists outside the main panel also give key panel benefits. Each insurer lists its panel on its website.
quote: policyholders can enjoy key panel benefits even if they seek treatment from selected specialists who are not on their insurer's main panel
can be found on their respective websites

lines.t: Asking your insurer to review and approve a planned treatment before it happens. Emergencies are excluded.
quote: Pre-authorisation is a process by which the policyholder obtains a review and approval of a medical treatment from the insurer prior to the actual procedure
they are excluded from the pre-authorisation process

lines.t: It tells you the amount covered before treatment. Not every Shield insurer offers it: Income does not, and Singlife stopped on 9 September 2023.
quote: This allows policyholders to know the amount that is covered by the insurer prior to undergoing treatment
Income does not offer pre-authorisation
Singlife has ceased offering pre-authorisation as of 9 September 2023

lines.t: A rider's yearly co-payment cap applies only to panel or pre-authorised claims.
lines.quote: Co-payment cap only applies to eligible claims such as panel or pre-authorised claims

lines.t: A disability expected to last for good. DPS, for example, defines it as the inability to take part in any employment permanently, or the permanent loss of use of both eyes, two limbs, or one eye and one limb.
quote: the inability to take part in any employment permanently
the total permanent loss of physical function of both eyes, or two limbs, or one eye and one limb

lines.t: A term or whole life plan that includes TPD benefit pays its sum insured if you become TPD.
lines.quote: Pays the sum insured when you die or become “Totally and Permanently Disabled” if TPD benefit is provided

lines.t: Definitions and payment schedules vary across products and insurers, so read your policy's own.
lines.quote: Payment schedules and definitions of disability vary across products and insurers

glossary.label: How TPD differs from disability income

lines.t: In disability income insurance, how long you must stay disabled before the monthly payouts start. Nothing is paid for that time.
quote: There may be a deferment period of time during which nothing is payable from the policy
Payment usually starts after you have been continuously disabled for longer than the deferment period

lines.t: It is not the same as a waiting period, which counts from the day the cover starts: typically 90 days for some critical illnesses.
lines.quote: A waiting period, typically 90 days from start date of coverage

example.t: A plan with a 3-month deferred period. Off work for 2 months: nothing is paid. Off work for a year: payouts cover the time after the first 3 months.

lines.t: Term cover whose sum assured falls over the term and reaches zero at the end. It is often used to cover a housing loan. The other kind of term cover is fixed: the same amount throughout.
quote: Two types of term insurance: fixed or decreasing coverage
will reduce and become zero by the end of the term
those used to cover the default of a housing loan

lines.t: MoneySense lists mortgage reducing term assurance as cover that pays off the home loan if the main borrower dies.
lines.quote: pays off the mortgage if the mortgagor passes away

lines.t: For an HDB flat, HPS is CPF's own mortgage-reducing insurance.

example.t: You owe $400,000 on a 25-year home loan. A decreasing plan starts at about $400,000 and falls on a schedule meant to track the loan. A fixed term plan for $400,000 would still pay $400,000 in year 20, when much less is owed.

lines.t: CPF's mortgage-reducing insurance for HDB flat owners. On death, terminal illness or total permanent disability, it pays off the outstanding housing loan, up to the insured sum, to HDB or the bank.
quote: a mortgage-reducing insurance
settle the outstanding housing loan, up to the insured sum, with HDB or the mortgagee directly

lines.t: It covers an HDB loan or a bank loan on an HDB flat. It is required if you pay the instalments with CPF, and strongly encouraged if you pay cash.
quote: If you're taking a bank loan, you can submit an online application to apply for HPS
If you're using CPF savings to pay your monthly housing instalments, HPS is required
If you're using cash, we strongly encourage you to apply

lines.t: It does not cover private property, ECs or privatised HUDC flats, and it ends at 65 or when the loan is paid off. For a loan on private property, or one running past 65, CPF suggests private insurance.
quote: It insures members until he/she turns 65, or until the housing loans are paid up
If you've an outstanding housing loan for a private property, consider purchasing private insurance coverage
do consider getting private insurance coverage after your HPS cover ends at 65

lines.t: Each owner's share of cover should at least match their share of the instalments, and a household's shares should add up to at least 100%. Acceptance depends on your health.
quote: Your share of the HPS cover should at least match the proportion of the monthly housing instalment
The total share of cover per household should add up to at least 100%
Your eligibility for an HPS cover is subject to approval and you being in good health

example.t: Two owners each pay half the instalments with CPF and each take half the cover. If one dies, HPS pays off half of what is still owed, and the other owner keeps paying the rest.

lines.t: A waiver of premium rider lets you stop paying a policy's premiums if you become disabled.
lines.quote: disability waiver of premium, which allows you to stop paying premiums for a policy if you become disabled

lines.t: When a parent buys a policy for a child, the parent is the policyholder and the child is the insured.
lines.quote: The parent is the policyholder and the child, the insured

lines.t: A payor rider puts the waiver on the parent who pays, so the child's premiums stop if the parent dies or becomes disabled (some riders also cover critical illness), and the child stays covered. Insurers name it differently, such as "payer benefit": read the rider's own wording.
LIA standardises only the severe stage of 37 common critical illnesses.
lines.quote: The LIA's common definitions describe the respective medical conditions at the “severe” stage

lines.t: Earlier, milder stages are worded by each insurer, so claims are not judged on identical definitions across insurers.
quote: are not standardised and are worded by each insurer
Claims assessment across insurers will not be based on identical definitions

lines.t: Some plans pay a smaller amount for an earlier stage of cancer.
lines.quote: Some critical illness policies pay a smaller amount for earlier stages of cancer

lines.t: LIA's 2024 update to the severe-stage definitions does not change an early-stage policy or rider you already hold.
lines.quote: your existing early stage CI policy or rider is not impacted

lines.t: A plan that can pay more than once, for example on diagnosis of different covered illnesses, up to the sum insured or the policy's limits.
lines.quote: make several payments upon diagnosis of different insured critical illnesses, subject to the sum insured or policy limits

lines.t: Before buying, check how long you must wait between claims and whether a relapse of the same illness counts.

faq.q: Can I cancel a new policy?
faq.short: Yes: within 14 days, or 21 days for a Shield plan.
faq.a: Send the insurer written notice within 14 days of receiving the policy, or 21 days for an Integrated Shield Plan. You get your premiums back minus any medical and other costs the insurer has already incurred.

faq.short: Guaranteed benefits are protected, with caps on life policies.
faq.a: The Policy Owners' Protection Scheme (run by SDIC) protects guaranteed benefits. For individual life policies it caps cover at S$500,000 of sum assured and S$100,000 of surrender value per life per insurer. Accident and health policies are protected without caps.

faq.q: How do I dispute a rejected claim?
faq.short: Insurer first, then FIDReC within six months.
faq.a: Go to the insurer first. If it is not resolved, file with FIDReC within six months of the insurer's final reply.

faq.q: Can I pay premiums with CPF?
faq.short: National schemes yes; Shield top-ups and supplements only up to limits.
faq.a: MediShield Life, CareShield Life and DPS premiums can be paid from CPF. IP top-ups are capped by MediSave Additional Withdrawal Limits, CareShield supplements by $600 a year.

faq.short: Simple plans sold without advice or commission, so cheaper.
faq.a: Simple term and whole life plans, with optional CI rider, sold directly without advice or commission. Their names start with "DIRECT" and you can compare them on compareFIRST.

faq.q: Where do I see what I already have?
faq.short: On the CPF Healthcare dashboard, with Singpass.
faq.a: Log in to the CPF Healthcare dashboard with Singpass to see your MediShield Life, IP, CareShield Life and ElderShield cover.

faq.q: Is the grace period for late premiums fixed?
faq.short: Usually 30 days. Check your own policy.
faq.a: Usually 30 days after the due date, during which the policy stays in force. Check your own policy.

pain_points.title: Too little cover for death and critical illness

key.l: of the critical illness cover needed by working Singaporeans and PRs with dependants was missing in 2022 (21% for death)
key.quote: who have at least one dependent

why.t: The average policyholder had critical illness cover of about 2.1 times annual income, and death cover of about 3.6 times.
quote: approximately 2.1 times of average annual income
approximately 3.6 times of average annual income

why.t: The MoneySense rule of thumb is 4 times income for critical illness and 9 times for death and TPD.

fix.t: Work out your own target, then count what you already hold, including DPS and any employer cover.
fix.label: Open the Cover check

fix.t: If you only need protection, term insurance gives the most cover for the money.
fix.quote: If you only need protection coverage, consider insurance-only term policies, which cost less

pain_points.title: A claim refused over a health condition you did not declare

key.l: of Shield plan claims were approved in 2019. Most refusals were for things the plan did not cover, such as excluded pre-existing conditions.

why.t: Leave out important facts on the application and the policy may not be valid.
why.quote: any policy issued may not be valid

why.t: Insurers check your medical records at claim time. If they show symptoms, advice or treatment before the cover started, the exclusion applies even if you did not know.
why.quote: had signs or symptoms, or had received advice, diagnosis or treatment before commencement of the insurance

fix.t: Declare everything the form asks for. If you are not sure a fact matters, declare it anyway.
fix.quote: If you are not sure whether a fact is important, you should disclose it anyway

fix.t: Read the completed form before you sign, even if an adviser filled it in.
fix.quote: Check that all relevant information you have provided is included in the proposal form

pain_points.title: A Shield plan you can no longer afford in old age

key.l: your MediShield Life premium: what a Shield plan can cost in your 70s or 80s

why.t: MediSave pays the private part only up to $300 a year at 40 and below (age next birthday), $600 from 41 to 70 and $900 from 71. The rest is cash.
Rider premiums are cash only and rise as you get older.
why.quote: The premium for riders must be paid with cash

fix.t: Choose the ward class you would really use. Aiming higher means paying more premiums than you need to.
fix.quote: or you'll end up paying more premiums than necessary

fix.t: If premiums get too high, move to a lower-ward plan with the same insurer. That needs no new health checks.
fix.quote: this would not need additional underwriting

pain_points.title: Switching plans and losing cover you already had

key.l: is what still covers a condition you already have after you switch to another Shield plan
key.quote: you will only be covered for pre-existing conditions up to MediShield Life benefits

why.t: A new health plan usually excludes conditions you already have, so switching can lose cover the old plan gave you.
why.quote: you may lose coverage for them if you switch to a new IP

why.t: Replacing a life policy can mean a penalty, new costs, and less cover for the same premium. Ending one in the early years is costly.
why.quote: It may be costly to terminate and replace a product in the early years

fix.t: If an adviser suggests cancelling a policy to buy another, ask why, and do not buy if the answer does not convince you.
fix.quote: Do not buy the product if you are uncomfortable with the recommendation

fix.t: Keep the old policy until the new one is in force.

pain_points.title: Paying for savings when what you needed was cover

key.l: is the most to spend on protection. Bundled plans like whole life may go past it.

why.t: Whole life, endowment and investment-linked plans mix savings with cover, so they cost more than term.
why.quote: Some products have an investment component to help you build savings

why.t: Ending a whole life policy early loses money.
why.quote: Early termination causes you to lose money

fix.t: If your budget is tight, buy term cover first.
fix.quote: If your budget is tight, get term insurance

fix.t: Direct Purchase Insurance plans are sold without advice or commission, so premiums are lower. Their names start with "DIRECT".
fix.quote: no commission is charged and you pay lower premiums than comparable life insurance products
